subject: Post-call: quantifying latency/throughput breakpoints + next steps
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@novacorp.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Khan <samir.khan@novacorp.com>
Date: Fri, Aug 28, 2026 at 3:12 PM PDT
Subject: Re: Intro + perf goals

Thanks for the call today — helpful discussion. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying numbers so you can recommend the right path (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private):

- Expected traffic profile: peak concurrency ~ 60 concurrent requests (spiky), sustained average ~ 12 rps.
- Payload profile: short prompts (~30-60 tokens) for classification/reranking, a smaller subset (~120 tokens) for summarization.
- Target SLOs: end-to-end p95 latency <= 250 ms for the classification path, and p95 <= 400 ms for summarize flows during peak.
- Cost sensitivity: if Dedicated committed capacity is >20% more expensive than Hosted at our volumes after optimizations, we need a strong latency case to justify it.
- Security: we may need VPC peering for production (later phase), but initial focus is on perf and cost.

Next steps we want from Redwood: concrete breakeven numbers showing at what throughput or latency thresholds Dedicated becomes cost-justified vs Hosted; a short proposal for a 2–3 week perf PoC (what you'll run, what we need to provide).

Can you and your SE run a quick comparison and propose a minimal MAP? Thanks — Elena

--
Elena Ruiz
Head of Engineering, NovaCorp

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@novacorp.com>
Cc: Samir Khan <samir.khan@novacorp.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, Aug 28, 2026 at 4:05 PM PDT
Subject: Re: Post-call: quantifying latency/throughput breakpoints + next steps

Elena — thanks for the clear numbers; very helpful. Quick recap and proposed plan from our side:

1) What we heard (aligned): peak ~60 concurrent/12 rps sustained; p95 targets 250ms (classify) / 400ms (summaries). VPC later. Cost sensitive.

2) Our offer: two-parallel PoC tracks so you can see tradeoffs quickly:
   - Hosted API benchmark: run with your representative payloads against our hosted endpoints with a dedicated test window (no code changes on your side). Measure p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and cost per million tokens.
   - Dedicated capacity estimate + lab run: sizing and cost model for a small Dedicated pool sized for your peak, plus an internal lab run (on the same model variant) to show the latency/throughput envelope.

3) Deliverables (2-week hands-on + 1 week analysis):
   - Mutual Action Plan (attached) that lists responsibilities and timelines.
   - Benchmark instructions (attached) so your infra team can kick off the Hosted test quickly.
   - A breakeven cost worksheet comparing Hosted (with observed batching & caching) vs Dedicated committed pricing for your profile.

4) Ask from you: a short test account or an allowlist IP range for our Hosted run; representative payloads (JSON sample); a preferred 2–3 day window to run hosted load tests.

I'll loop in Dylan (SE) and Karthik (deployment lead) to propose exact test steps and a recommended Dedicated pool size. If that plan looks good, we can get the Hosted test started early next week.

Thanks — Hannah
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena@novacorp.com>, Samir Khan <samir.khan@novacorp.com>
Date: Sat, Aug 29, 2026 at 09:10 AM PDT
Subject: RE: Post-call: quantifying latency/throughput breakpoints + next steps

Thanks Hannah / Elena — putting proposed bench steps below so Elena & Samir know what we'll run and what we need from NovaCorp.

Planned steps (Hosted benchmark):
- Run three 30-minute windows: ramp (10m), sustained (15m), cool-down (5m).
- Payloads: classification (30–60 tokens) @ 70% traffic; summarization (120 tokens) @ 30%.
- Metrics collected: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, successful requests/s, observed batching factor, cost estimate (tokens x pricing).
- Requirements from NovaCorp: allowlist 3 Redwood load IPs OR a short-lived API key for a test namespace; sample payloads (we provide schema).

Dedicated estimate methodology (what we will deliver internally):
- Using your peak concurrency we model a Dedicated GPU pool (N GPUs) and run an internal load fixture to estimate p95 latency at different concurrency points.
- We'll produce a breakeven chart: X axis = concurrent requests, Y axis = cost per 1M tokens (Hosted vs Dedicated).

Timing: Can start Hosted run as early as Mon, Aug 31 if Elena can provide allowlist/API key and sample payloads by EOD Mon. Deliverables (to you): MAP + bench report + breakeven chart by Fri, Sep 10 (includes analysis).

Attachments: benchmark-instructions.md (contains CLI snippets), cost-model.csv (templated sheet).

Notes for internal ops (Dev & Karthik): please confirm if SRE needs to be engaged for VPC-specific notes — Elena said VPC is “later phase” but might affect network design. Also, Karthik, can you draft a Dedicated sizing recommendation (N GPUs and expected throughput) so we can present a clear tradeoff?

-Dylan
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena@novacorp.com>
Date: Sun, Aug 30, 2026 at 9:40 AM PDT
Subject: RE: Post-call: quantifying latency/throughput breakpoints + next steps

Quick internal note and commitment:

- I'll produce a short two-slide recommendation by EOD Mon, Sept 1: 1) latency breakpoints (where Hosted p95 diverges from Dedicated for the given payloads), 2) cost breakeven table (assumptions called out).
- Dev: can you confirm whether we need SRE to pre-authorize any VPC-specific network flows? If not required now, we will still include the VPC gating items in the MAP.
- Hannah: I'll prep the Dedicated sizing as "recommended starting pool" + an alternative with autoscaling headroom.

Elena — we'll keep the Hosted bench non-invasive; you'll only need to provide allowlist or a short-lived test key and the sample payloads.

Karthik
Deployment Lead, Redwood Inference
